edits.current: Simple S.A. offers to build the severance savings return from the contributor list of the last PILA return paid for the chosen year. Convenient and dangerous: the PILA population is the population that was PAID in a month, which is not the population ENTITLED to a severance savings deposit for the year - leavers who left in June are absent from the December PILA but are still owed a pro rata deposit, and all-inclusive salary employees are present in PILA but owed nothing. The engine must generate the population itself and set this to N.
edits.proposed: Simple S.A. offers to build the severance savings return from the contributor list of the last PILA return paid for the chosen year. Convenient and dangerous: the PILA population is the population that was PAID in a month, which is not the population ENTITLED to a severance savings deposit for the year. An employee who left during the accrual year is EXCLUDED from the deposit: the severance savings are paid directly in the final settlement (Ley 50 de 1990 art. 99 num. 4; Population Rules Step 0 exclusion (2)), so a leaver must never be added to the return - a leaver included is a double payment. All-inclusive salary employees are present in PILA but owed nothing, and the other Step 0 exclusions are not visible in a PILA list either. The engine must generate the population itself from the Population Rules and set this to N. CLIENT DATA (Accumulated Report): all 10 employees whose last salary fell in Oct-Dec 2025 received severance savings and interest directly through WT 62110 'Cash-out of Severance Pay' and WT 62117 'Cash-out of Interest Severance Pay' in the termination month or the month after, and none has a February-2026 fund payment (WT 25827); the 103 integral-salary employees (WT 62140) likewise carry no 25827 - both exclusions are confirmed by the client's practice.
edits.reason: Decision 5: the spec contradicted itself (E08 and Report Matrix said a June leaver is owed a pro rata deposit; Population Rules Step 0 excludes leavers); the legal rule is Ley 50 de 1990 art. 99 num. 4 and the client's Q4-2025 leavers confirm it.

edits.current: Mandatory. Admits values from 1 to 360 - a 360-DAY COMMERCIAL YEAR, not 365. A full year of service is 360, and every partial year is the actual days of service counted on the commercial convention (each month 30 days). Include the days of paid leave and of employer-paid or institution-paid incapacity, which count as service. The 3-position field cannot carry more than one year, which is the layout's way of saying that this filing is strictly one accrual year per record.

SOURCE AND EXCLUSIONS: per Population Rules Step 1, count the accrual-year days of service on the 30-day convention from the later of 1 January and the current-contract hire date to the earlier of 31 December and the leaving date, EXCLUDING unpaid leave and suspensions. The December balance 68028 equals 'ces base' 68040 x 68029 / 360 for 204 of 284 employees; for the others the difference is consistent with in-year direct payments (62110), but this can only be verified from the Accumulated Report for payments from October 2025 onwards, because earlier months fall outside its window. Use 68029 only as a reconciliation check, not as the source: it shows 0 for a late-December hire (16-12-2025) who was nevertheless deposited for 15 days, and for early-2025 hires it differs from the commercial count from the hire date (300 for a 10-02-2025 hire, while the client's own interest 62127 for the same employee uses 321 days; 300 vs 314 for a 17-02-2025 hire).

edits.field_name: Basic salary reported in the last month
edits.current: SCOPE ROUTING (v1.1 alignment patch): the amount is owned by the Wage Type Catalogue, not the Data Dictionary - the pipeline scope rule routes 'Base Salary / Basic Salary amounts -> WTC, NOT DD'. The 'Payroll.' prefix marks it as outside DD master data; it is a standing contract attribute, not a per-run computation. Column E is therefore N and the Data Dictionary correctly holds no Contractual Salary field. Mandatory. Nine integers, no decimals, no commas, no points, not less than zero. The layout is explicit about WHICH salary: 'el ultimo basic salary reportado en el mes de diciembre del ano accrued de severance savings'. THIS IS THE OPERATOR'S REPORTING FIELD, NOT THE STATUTORY BASE. CST art. 253 fixes the statutory base as the last monthly salary provided it has not varied in the last three months, otherwise the average of the last year of service (or of the whole period if shorter), INCLUDING the transport allowance. The field name says 'basico' and the operator's calculator uses it alone - see the trap documented at T14. Report the December basic here and compute T14 yourself.

edits.field_name: Value of the severance savings deposited
edits.current: Mandatory, nine integers. TWO RULES AND ONE TRAP. Rule one, the floor: 'el value minimo del collection debe ser de un (1) dia de un (1) SMLMV del ano accrued' - for accrual year 2026 one day of the SMMLV of COP 1,750,905 is COP 58,363.50, so a record below that is rejected. Rule two, the override: the layout's own formula is basic salary * (dias worked / 360) BUT 'en este campo el contributor puede especificar un value diferente y no se haran calculos automaticos de este value'. THE TRAP: the operator's formula omits the TRANSPORT ALLOWANCE, which CST art. 253 requires in the base. For an employee on the 2026 minimum wage the operator would compute 1,750,905 while the statute requires (1,750,905 + 249,095) = 2,000,000 - a shortfall of COP 249,095 that is a SHORT DEPOSIT, penalised at one day's salary for every day of delay under Law 50 of 1990 art. 99 num. 3, uncapped. ALWAYS write the engine's own figure into this field and never rely on the portal calculator. Where the monthly advance regime of MA01 is in use, this field carries the CONSOLIDATED annual figure and only the difference computed at MA05 is actually deposited in February.
edits.proposed: Mandatory, nine integers. TWO RULES AND ONE TRAP. Rule one, the floor: 'el value minimo del collection debe ser de un (1) dia de un (1) SMLMV del ano accrued' - for accrual year 2026 one day of the SMMLV of COP 1,750,905 is COP 58,363.50, so a record below that is rejected. Rule two, the override: the layout's own formula is basic salary * (dias worked / 360) BUT 'en este campo el contributor puede especificar un value diferente y no se haran calculos automaticos de este value'. THE TRAP: the operator's formula omits the TRANSPORT ALLOWANCE, which CST art. 253 requires in the base. For an employee on the 2026 minimum wage the operator would compute 1,750,905 while the statute requires (1,750,905 + 249,095) = 2,000,000 - a shortfall of COP 249,095 that is a SHORT DEPOSIT, penalised at one day's salary for every day of delay under Law 50 of 1990 art. 99 num. 3, uncapped. ALWAYS write the engine's own figure into this field and never rely on the portal calculator. Where the monthly advance regime of MA01 is in use, this field carries the CONSOLIDATED annual figure and only the difference computed at MA05 is actually deposited in February. WHAT IS DEPOSITED - NET OF DIRECT PAYMENTS ALREADY MADE: T14 carries the amount actually deposited for the employee = the consolidated 31 December balance (IN01) LESS the lawful partial payments already made directly to the employee during the accrual year (CST art. 254; Population Rules Step 1 (f)) and LESS any direct payment of that balance made in January to an employee who left before the deposit, which is lawful under Ley 50 de 1990 art. 99 num. 4. An employee who left and was paid in full in the final settlement is not in the return at all (Population Rules Step 0 exclusion (2)). Keep the gross annual liquidation as a separate engine value: System Mapping 'Cesantias_Annual_Liquidation' is the gross figure, T14 is the net deposit. CLIENT EVIDENCE (Accumulated Report): the February payroll carries 25827 / 65805 'Payment Severance Funds Inf.' for 236 employees, in 01/02/2026 only. For 280 of 282 employees with a deposit or a January advance, 25827 (Feb) + 62126 'Advance Severance Last Year' (Jan) = the absolute value of 63814 'Severance Balance (Current Month)' in January, i.e. the consolidated 31 December balance (the 2 exceptions are late-December hires with no January balance). That balance is the annual liquidation ('ces base' 68040 x days / 360) less the in-year direct payments 62110 'Cash-out of Severance Pay' (110 employees carry 62110 and 62117 in the 12-month window; e.g. 2,120,000 in Nov-2025, balance 9,051,613 = 11,171,613 - 2,120,000); this deduction can be reproduced from the report for 174 of 285 balances only, because payments made in Jan-Sep 2025 fall outside its window. 54 employees received part of the consolidated balance directly in January via 62126 and only the remainder was deposited (e.g. balance 16,074,021: 16,000,000 via 62126 and 74,021 via 25827); the reports examined do not split these 54 between employees who had left and employees still in service, and whether such a January payment to an employee STILL IN SERVICE lawfully reduces T14 is pending RA confirmation (see Query to RA) - the engine must not copy that practice until RA confirms it. Where the remainder after direct payments falls below the one-day SMMLV floor the channel would reject the record - treatment pending RA. The client base 68040 exceeds the December basic salary 63807 for 202 of the 236 depositees (variable pay averaged under CST art. 253), which confirms that T14 must never be left to the operator's basic-salary formula.
edits.reason: Decision 5 (deposit net of direct payments already made; January payment to a leaver lawful; leaver excluded) with the verifier's figures (280/282, 236, 54, 174/285, 110, 202/236); the in-service January case stays a query.
edits.vc_sentence: T14: the value deposited is the consolidated 31 December balance net of the direct payments already made to the employee (CST art. 254 in-year partial payments; Ley 50 de 1990 art. 99 num. 4 for an employee who left before the deposit), evidenced by WT 25827 + WT 62126 = |WT 63814| for 280 of 282 employees; the treatment of a January partial payment to an employee still in service stays an RA query.

edits.current: The employee's residential address, 50 positions, left-aligned and space-filled. This is the AFFILIATE'S address for the fund's own statutory communications with its member, which is why the layout asks for the residence and not the work address - contrast electronic payroll and PILA, which carry the WORK municipality. Do not send the work address; the fund will post the member's statements to it. Composite Key: the affiliate's domicile is carried across THREE fields that must describe one place - T15 the free-text street address, T16 the two-digit DANE department and T17 the three-digit DANE municipality. Within T15 itself, Colombian addresses decompose as via type (CALLE / CARRERA / DIAGONAL / TRANSVERSAL), via number, the NO separator, the cross-via number, the hyphen, the door number and any complement (APTO / TORRE / INT). Abbreviate by a documented rule where the whole exceeds 50 positions - never cut mid-token, because the fund cannot repair a truncated address.

edits.field_name: Annual interest on severance savings at 12%
edits.current: 12% per annum on the IN01 balance, pro-rated on days over 360. PAID TO THE EMPLOYEE DIRECTLY, IN THE MONTH OF JANUARY of the following year - not to the fund, and not in February. The two obligations have different payees, different deadlines and different penalties: failure to deposit the principal costs one day's salary per day of delay, whereas failure to pay the interest costs an indemnity equal to the interest owed, ONCE ONLY (Law 52 of 1975 art. 1). The draft decree would add a further precision at art. 4: the interest is 'entregado directamente al employee dentro del mes siguiente a la fecha de liquidacion del auxilio de cesantia'. No interest on interest may be liquidated.

edits.current: CST art. 57 para. 4, added by Law 2466 of 2025 art. 15, verbatim: 'Cuando el employer acredite de manera fehaciente el payment directo al employee del value correspondiente a las severance savings, dicho payment se considerara liberatorio de la obligacion, y no procedera sancion por no consignacion, salvo que se demuestre que el payment no se realizo en condiciones de libertad y que no fue utilizado en fines autorizados por la Law. No obstante, la afiliacion a Severance-savings fund es mandatory.' Three limits the engine must respect: the discharge needs FEHACIENTE evidence, it is rebuttable on the freedom-and-purpose test, and it does NOT remove the duty to affiliate the employee to a fund. A DRAFTING NOTE on the citation: art. 15's enacting formula announces only 'los paragrafos 2 y 3' of CST art. 57, yet the published text prints a Paragrafo 4 and this is it - so cite CST art. 57 para. 4 as added by Law 2466 of 2025 art. 15, and expect the discrepancy to be raised.

CLIENT PRACTICE - DIRECT PAYMENTS AND THE DEPOSIT: the client pays part of the severance savings directly to the employee (62110 'Cash-out of Severance Pay' during the year, 110 employees in the 12-month window; 62126 'Advance Severance Last Year' in January, 54 employees) and deposits only the remainder (25827) - e.g. masked employee 27114435, balance 9,051,613: 8,466,400 via 62126 in January and 585,213 via 25827 in February. This flag covers a FULL discharge of the deposit obligation by proven direct payment (Population Rules Step 0 exclusion (4)). An employee who left and was paid directly in the final settlement is NOT an E92 case but a Step 0 exclusion (2) under Ley 50 de 1990 art. 99 num. 4, and a January direct payment to an employee who left before the deposit is treated as that lawful payment. A partial direct payment does not set E92 = Y: T14 carries the deposit net of the direct payments already made and the record is still produced. Whether a January direct payment of part of the consolidated balance to an employee who REMAINS in service is a lawful partial payment or a CST art. 57 para. 4 direct payment needing fehaciente evidence is pending RA confirmation (see T14 and Query to RA).
